title: macOS No Internet
scenario: Ms. Chen brings her MacBook Pro (Apple Silicon, macOS 14.6) to the IT office in person before a department meeting. The machine cannot reach any websites. She can see the Wi-Fi network and is connected, but Safari shows 'Cannot connect to server' for all sites.
impact: Instructional: A department meeting with 8 science teachers cannot proceed with their planned presentation if the presenting teacher's laptop is offline.
objectives: Test DNS resolution from the MacBook
Verify the network path with ping and traceroute
Distinguish between a device-side issue and a network-side issue
Restore connectivity or isolate the cause
Document the troubleshooting steps and resolution

evidence.description: Output of ping to 8.8.8.8 and an internal IP
DNS resolution test for a known hostname
Browser error message or behavior observed

decisionPoints.prompt: Ping to 8.8.8.8 succeeds but Safari cannot load any website. What is the most likely cause?

options.label: DNS resolution is broken — the machine can reach the internet but cannot look up domain names
options.feedback: Correct — this is the classic signature: ping works but HTTP fails because DNS cannot resolve names.

options.label: A proxy server is configured and is unreachable
options.feedback: Possible in a school environment — check the proxy settings.

options.label: The access point's uplink is down
options.feedback: If the uplink were down, ping to 8.8.8.8 would also fail.

ticket.initialDescription: MacBook Pro (Apple Silicon, macOS 14.6) cannot load any websites. Wi-Fi connected but browsers show 'Cannot connect to server'.

nodes.title: Greet and acknowledge
nodes.body: Welcome Ms. Chen. Confirm the issue and note the time constraint. Do not rush into changing settings — first understand the exact symptoms.

nodes.title: Reproduce the issue
nodes.body: Open Safari and attempt to load a known site. Note the exact error. Check if this is a single-site issue or affects all sites.

nodes.title: Gather network evidence
nodes.body: Run ping, DNS lookup, and traceroute from Terminal. Document the output as evidence. Check the DNS server settings in System Settings.

nodes.title: Identify the root cause
nodes.body: Based on the evidence, choose the most likely cause of the connectivity issue.

nodes.title: State hypothesis
nodes.body: State your hypothesis in one sentence. What do you think is broken, and what evidence supports it?

nodes.title: Fix the DNS issue
nodes.body: Correct the DNS configuration on Ms. Chen's MacBook.

nodes.title: Validate
nodes.body: Re-test DNS resolution. Have Ms. Chen open Safari and load the presentation site. Confirm full connectivity is restored.

nodes.title: Document and close
nodes.body: Write a ticket resolution with root cause, steps, and validation.
nodes.prompt: Write a follow-up message to Ms. Chen.

kbOpportunity: macOS DNS troubleshooting — commands and settings to check when browsers fail but ping succeeds.
